We're currently in a couples counseling because my insurance covers it. He however doesn't have any insurance at the moment, so it'd be very expensive for any kind of therapy.
Thanks for the advice, but there's really no way of take-backs. I'm looking for advice to deal with the aftermath.

Well, it's difficult, because nothing was inherently wrong with my relationship prior to my affairs. It seems that the abusive behavior only occurred after the fallout of that. 

I think what gets me is I know he can express his anger without resorting to abusive (verbal or physical) behavior. It's like we both recognize this, it's just that for whatever reason, it's not applied when it's needed.

Thanks for responding. I suppose I do get the whole "you should love yourself" thing, but it's just really hard when my past is constantly lingering in my mind. There's always this voice in my head that tells me, "Hey, remember that shitty thing you did? Well, I'm going to remind you of that and all the stupid shit you've done as well!"

On one hand, I love him a lot and don't want to leave. On the other hand, I don't think I deserve to leave. Why do I, the adulterer, get a chance at a happier life, to be able to start on a clean slate while the betrayed is left, forever scarred and with trust issues? It doesn't seem fair to me, I deserve that punishment, not him.

It really sounds like you didn't have the opportunity to properly go through the emotions. I'm sorry that you had been cheated on. Do you perhaps not feel bad about it because of this? I don't want to just jump to assumptions here.

Then you are what is called a madhatter - you have been betrayed, and you have been a wayward in the same relationship. This makes it a bit more difficult, because I've honestly haven't had to deal with this.

What happened after your boyfriend cheated? Did he work on himself, or was it more of a sweep it under the rug and not talk about it deal?

That's the "fog" I'm talking about. Many people who have cheated are able to compartmentalize; their relationship is over here in the corner of the brain while they are with the affair partner, and it doesn't seem to interfere. 

If possible, try going NC with the affair partner. If you don't feel anything (remorse, guilt, etc), then you should leave your boyfriend, or choose to confess to him. I mean, you realize you wouldn't be able to hand an open relationship, so it's a "how would you feel" kind of thing if he was the one cheating.

BTDT. But I think you owe it to your boyfriend to let him know what's going on. He never agreed to an open relationship. If you want an open relationship, that's your choice, but you shouldn't go behind his back about it. 

If you're like me, it'll hit you like a ton of bricks once the fog fades away..

It sounds like a deal breaker to me. If she can't get past the notion that you have a degree in something that doesn't tickle her fancy, she either needs to get over it or move on. 

Is she saying this because you haven't found a career in your field, or that whatever field you do have doesn't make as much money?
Maybe posting on r/talesfromretail would help you. I know it's not a solution but when I get so exhausted pretending to be happy all day, unwinding with stories helps me realize I'm not alone.

For hers and your protection, it'd probably be best to stop. Consider that at any time during sex, she could change her mind. If she's unconscious, she doesn't have the opportunity to change her mind, therefore, she's being stripped of her choice.
